_comment: CUDA extension packages that commonly fail to install, and why. `releases` rows apply from their version up to the next row; a pin that matches a row exactly uses that row. `platforms` lists where PyPI has a binary wheel (os-arch); anywhere else pip compiles the sdist. `torch` is the requirement that release's wheels declare on torch (its compiled kernels are tied to that torch ABI). Wheel and torch data verified against https://pypi.org/pypi/<package>/json and https://pypi.org/pypi/xformers/<version>/json (requires_dist). flash-attn, mamba-ssm and causal-conv1d publish only sdists whose setup.py imports torch, which fails under build isolation (https://discuss.huggingface.co/t/170972, https://github.com/Dao-AILab/flash-attention#installation-and-features). bitsandbytes shipped Linux-only binaries inside `any` wheels before 0.43.0, added win_amd64 in 0.43.0, linux aarch64 in 0.46.0, macOS arm64 in 0.49.0 and win_arm64 in 0.50.0.

packages.name: flash-attn
packages.build_note: On Linux its setup.py first tries to download a prebuilt wheel from the flash-attention GitHub releases for the exact torch, CUDA and Python in use, and compiles only when none matches.
packages.alternative: PyTorch's built-in scaled_dot_product_attention covers most uses: in transformers pass attn_implementation="sdpa". On Windows, WSL2 gets the Linux prebuilt wheels.

packages.name: mamba-ssm
packages.build_note: On Linux its setup.py first tries to download a prebuilt wheel from the mamba GitHub releases for the exact torch, CUDA and Python in use, and compiles only when none matches.
packages.alternative: transformers' Mamba models fall back to a slower pure-PyTorch path when mamba-ssm is absent. On Windows, use WSL2.

packages.name: causal-conv1d
packages.build_note: On Linux its setup.py first tries to download a prebuilt wheel from the causal-conv1d GitHub releases for the exact torch, CUDA and Python in use, and compiles only when none matches.
packages.alternative: It is optional for mamba-ssm and transformers' Mamba models, which fall back to a PyTorch implementation without it. On Windows, use WSL2.

packages.name: xformers
packages.alternative: PyTorch 2's built-in scaled_dot_product_attention replaces most xformers memory-efficient attention (diffusers and transformers use it by default).

packages.name: bitsandbytes
packages.alternative: Upgrade to bitsandbytes 0.43.0+ for native Windows wheels, or 0.49.0+ for Apple Silicon (macOS 14+). Intel Macs have no build; skip 8-bit/4-bit quantization there.
